headline: Indian startup Quanfluence raised $10 million to build a light-based quantum computer, starting with a four-qubit machine.
score_reason: Small round and early-stage; the 100x speed claim is the company's own.
importance_line: Indian deep-tech investors and researchers gain a new photonic quantum builder, but it has only a four-qubit goal and its speed claim is unverified.
summary: Entrackr reports, citing a company press release, that Bengaluru-based Quanfluence raised $10 million in a round led by Chiratae Ventures to build a four-qubit photonic quantum computer, a machine that uses light and works at room temperature, with a roughly 100-qubit prototype targeted for 2029. The company's claim that its system can be up to 100 times faster than classical computing for some optimisation tasks is its own and unverified.
notes: Pool link (Economic Times) returned no text; same story read at Entrackr. Category set to MKT (funding round) from default RES.
